name: drover
summary: Race a runner to the far row.
A turn is two parts, in either order: move one of your runners, and, if you like, move the boulder.
The boulder in the middle belongs to nobody. It steps one square any way and crushes an enemy runner it steps onto. Nothing can take it.
Runners step straight or diagonally forward, and take only diagonally forward.
You may move the boulder first only if a runner move is left for you after it. A player with no legal turn loses.
description: A race in which every turn has two parts. Two rows of runners face each other, each side trying to get one runner to the far row, and between them sits a boulder that belongs to nobody. On your turn you must move a runner, and you may also move the boulder, before the runner or after it. The boulder steps one square in any direction and crushes an enemy runner it steps onto, and nothing may take it. Because the boulder move is extra rather than instead, it is never a tempo lost: the question is which order and where to leave it, since your opponent will drive the same boulder on their turn. Boulder first clears or blocks the square your runner wants; runner first lets the boulder follow up behind it. You may also leave the boulder where it stands, which is sometimes the only safe place for it.

provenance.history: Q1133 (TS3, docs/plan-tessabi.md section 3): the showcase for rules.turn.parts and rules.turn.order.
